missions.title: Compare insulation labels at a hardware store
missions.description: Visit a hardware store or its website and compare the labels and product sheets for a few kinds of insulation, such as cellulose, mineral wool, fiberglass and foam board. Note what each is made of and anything the maker says about recycled content, then turn your notes into a simple comparison chart. Post a photo of your chart.
missions.proof_hint: A photo of your comparison chart, with product types and what each is made of.
missions.safety: Look at packaging and product sheets only; don't open packages or handle loose fibers, which can irritate skin and lungs.
missions.about: Deploy Alternative Insulation Materials is defined as using alternative building insulation materials in place of conventional ones. In particular, we highlight the impact of using cellulose instead of glass, mineral, or plastic insulation in new and retrofit buildings.

missions.title: Find out which refrigerant your fridge uses
missions.description: Look for the rating label on your fridge or freezer, often inside the door or on an inner wall, which names the refrigerant it uses. Look up that refrigerant from an official or manufacturer source and write a sentence or two on what you learned. Post a photo of the label next to your note.
missions.proof_hint: A photo of the refrigerant label with your short note.
missions.safety: Read only labels you can see easily; don't move heavy appliances, unplug them or touch any tubing or sealed parts.
missions.about: This solution involves reducing the use of high-global warming potential (GWP) refrigerants, instead deploying lower-GWP refrigerants. High-GWP (>800 on a 100-yr basis) fluorinated gases (F-gases) are currently used as refrigerants in refrigeration, air conditioning, and heat pump systems. Over the lifetime of this equipment, refrigerants escape into the atmosphere where they contribute to climate change.

missions.title: Share how to safely get rid of an old fridge
missions.description: Find out how your city, county or utility handles old fridges, freezers and air conditioners, including any pickup or drop-off service that removes the refrigerant properly. Turn the official steps into a short, friendly post or flyer for your building or neighborhood group, with links to the official pages. Post a link or photo of what you shared.
missions.proof_hint: A link or photo of your post or flyer with the official sources listed.
missions.safety: Never cut, drain or vent refrigerant lines yourself, since only trained, certified technicians should handle refrigerant, and put up flyers only where you have permission.
missions.about: Improving refrigerant management involves deploying practices and technologies that reduce the amount of climate-warming refrigerant chemicals escaping into the atmosphere from air conditioning, refrigeration, and heat pump equipment. missions.title: Ask a public building how it controls its energy use
missions.description: Pick a public building you use, such as a library, school or community center, and send a short, polite question in your own words to its facilities office or the agency that runs it: does the building use automatic controls to schedule heating, cooling and lights, and who looks after them? missions.safety: Ask only through official public channels, and never enter staff-only areas or touch any controls or equipment.

missions.description: Find a friend, relative or neighbor who already heats their home with a heat pump and ask a few simple questions: how it handles cold and hot days, what surprised them, and what they wish they had known. missions.title: Help a neighbor set up their thermostat schedule
missions.description: If a family member or neighbor has a programmable or smart thermostat but has never set a schedule and would like help, sit down with them and read the manual together. Set times that keep the home comfortable when people are in and ease off when they are out or asleep, with the resident deciding every setting and doing any app sign-in themselves. missions.title: Map the drafty windows in your home
missions.description: On a cool or windy day, move slowly around each window you can reach from the floor and hold a strip of tissue paper near the edges; if it flutters, you have found a draft. Mark each drafty spot on a simple sketch of your home, and if you rent, you can share the list politely with your landlord or building manager. Post a photo of your sketch.
missions.proof_hint: A photo of your sketch or list showing which windows have drafts.
missions.safety: Use a tissue strip rather than a candle or lighter, and stay on the floor instead of climbing to reach high windows.
missions.about: We define Improve Windows & Glass as reducing the heat transferred through typical windows used in residential and nonresidential buildings by improving the thermal insulation capacity of the glass. Windows typically constitute a small portion of a building envelope but account for a substantial portion of the heat transferred (gained or lost) between the indoor space and the external environment.

missions.description: Visit a farmers market and, when stalls are quiet, ask a few farmers what they think about putting solar panels on farmland, including setups where crops grow or animals graze under the panels. missions.safety: Ask politely, accept no for an answer, and share names, photos or farm details only with permission.

missions.description: Many people who rent or live in apartments can't put panels on their own roof.
